items.title: 61427_Happy Caldwell oral history interview
items.q: But he was my favorite, Don was. He was such a fine guy.

ctx.x: And they were too -- I mean they didn't swing because they couldn't swing them.
No, they didn't. But he was my favorite, Don was. He was such a fine guy.

Yeah, but, you know, first time I came here in '37 Willie Bryant had a (unintelligible) that band at the Savoy. So my wife knew him, I think. Anyway, he came over and sat talking to us, that -- I said, who's playing that good trumpet solo there. He said, Sidney DeParis. I said, well, what's he doing in your band? He said, oh, he's very glad to be in my band. He said, he's just got out of Don Redman's band, and he said that was tearing his lips to pieces. So, he said, my band is much easier for him.
